UP to introduce GPS tracking of sugarcane transport vehicles

By
ChiniMandi
-
October 5, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:40
Instaread

Moradabad: Uttar Pradesh is set to introduce a Vehicle Tracking System (VTS) from the upcoming crushing season to monitor the movement of sugarcane transport vehicles and ensure timely delivery of cane to sugar mills, Hindustan reported.

Under the new system, vehicles transporting sugarcane from purchase centres to mills across the state will be tracked live through GPS. The move is aimed at making the cane transportation process more transparent and identifying delays or negligence in the movement of vehicles.

The Cane Development Department plans to ensure that sugarcane reaches the concerned mill within 24 hours of harvesting. Timely transportation is expected to help reduce weight loss caused by drying of cane and protect farmers from losses.

Deputy Cane Commissioner Harpal Singh said the initiative is being taken in line with the vision of Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and the Cane and Sugar Commissioner to modernise the functioning of the sugar industry and improve farmers’ welfare.

The department is linking the sugarcane supply chain with digital technology as part of efforts to streamline transportation. The VTS will provide live information on the movement of cane-carrying vehicles, enabling officials to monitor the transportation process more effectively.

The department said the system is being introduced for the first time across Uttar Pradesh. It is expected to improve coordination between cane purchase centres and sugar mills and ensure that harvested cane is transported within the stipulated time.

The initiative is also aimed at reducing losses arising from delays in transportation. By ensuring faster delivery of harvested cane to mills, the department expects to minimise weight loss due to drying and provide greater protection to farmers’ interests.
